newsitem.title: UK: UK report says older mums key to male infertility.
newsitem.headline: UK report says older mums key to male infertility.

text.p: British researchers are investigating whether rising male infertility is linked to the trend for women to wait until they are older to have children, the Sunday Times reported.
It said preliminary studies showed that men whose mothers waited to start a family until their late thirties or early forties were significantly likely to have poorer quality sperm.

Justin St John, a university researcher at Sheffield's Jessop Hospital for Women, said the sperm of men who were born to mothers over 40 were significantly less able to swim fast and straight than sperm of men born to mothers under 20.

The Sunday Times said scientists believed the results could be explained by genetic damage that accumulates with age inside structures within the mother's egg cells that are inherited by her children.

"The older the woman is, the more likely it is that the egg cell has undergone damage to her mitochondrial DNA. This could then be transmitted to her offspring and, in the case of the male, result in infertility," St John told the newspaper.
He said he was now collating information from fertility centres around Britain to further the research.
Previous research has suggested that declining male fertility could be related to chemical pollutants, tight underwear, or sedentary lifestyles.
